reports.title: REPORT OF FOREIGN PRIVATE ISSUER PURSUANT TO RULE 13a-16

lines: From 2027 through 2030, the Company expects to open 550 to 600 restaurants and to invest $1.3 billion to $1.5 billion in capital expenditures.

desk.headline: Revenue up 11% to $1.33bn, in line; EPS of $0.15 just below estimates; first $25m buyback; long-term targets repeated
results: Revenue rose 11.3% to $1.33bn (17.6% in constant currency), with comparable sales up 15.5% on higher checks and more guests.
Adjusted EBITDA was $125.9m; it fell 37% as reported because last year included an $85.6m Brazil tax credit, but rose 9% without it.
Profit fell to $31.2m ($0.15 a share) from $150.4m ($0.71), again mainly due to that one-off credit.
Food and paper costs improved 90bp as a share of revenue; digital sales grew about 22% to two-thirds of system sales.
The board approved a buyback of up to $25m over six months; net debt was 1.3 times EBITDA.

guidance.summary: There is no 2026 profit or revenue guidance. The company repeated its Investor Day targets for 2027–2030, which management called long-term averages, not yearly guidance.

points: The CEO said Q4 started solidly, with comparable sales trends normalising in October.
Brazil had its best guest-count growth in eight quarters; management was cautiously optimistic on Brazil margins.
Mexico remained tough but comparable sales were roughly flat, an improvement on Q2, with market share gains.
Wage inflation ran ahead of check growth in all three divisions; full-year payroll costs are seen broadly in line with 2025.
Management said it sees the shares as undervalued, explaining the buyback alongside spending, dividends and a healthy balance sheet.
